extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, third-party requesters, patent owners, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing, prosecuting, and appealing inter partes reexamination proceedings (documents, timing, content, service, limits on prior art, duties, and consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: <110> Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant name: if applicant is inventor, preferably max. of 10 names; one name per line; preferable format: Surname, Other Names and/or Initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M). Provide one name per line in the preferred format.

rubrics_metrics.name: <120> Title of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Title of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M).

rubrics_metrics.name: <130> File Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal file reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory when filed prior to assignment or application number; provide if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: <140> Current Application Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Current application number specified as: US 09/999,999 or PCT/US09/99999.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M) if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: <141> Current Filing Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Current filing date specified as yyyy-mm-dd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M) if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: <150> Prior Application Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior application number (e.g., US 09/999,999 or PCT/US09/99999).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M), if applicable include priority documents under 35 U.S.C. 119 and 120.

rubrics_metrics.name: <151> Prior Application Filing Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior application filing date specified as yyyy-mm-dd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M), if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: <160> Number of SEQ ID NOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Count includes total number of SEQ ID NOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M). Response shall be an integer representing the SEQ ID NO shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: <170> Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of software used to create the 'Sequence Listing'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional (O). Provide name of software if used.

rubrics_metrics.name: <210> SEQ ID NO:#
rubrics_metrics.description: SEQ ID NO label (e.g., 'SEQ ID NO:#').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M). SEQ ID NO should follow the numeric identifier and should appear on the line preceding the actual sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: <211> Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond with an integer expressing the number of bases or amino acid residues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M).

rubrics_metrics.name: <212> Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the presented sequence molecule is DNA, RNA, or PRT (protein). If a nucleotide sequence contains both DNA and RNA fragments, the type shall be 'DNA.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M). If combined DNA/RNA molecule, further described in <220>-<223>.

rubrics_metrics.name: <213> Organism
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific name, 'Unknown' or 'Artificial Sequence'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M) under conditions: if 'n', 'Xaa', or a modified/unusual L-amino acid or modified base was used; or if ORGANISM is 'Artificial Sequence' or 'Unknown'; or if molecule is combined DNA/RNA. If 'Unknown' or 'Artificial Sequence' provide further description in <220>-<223>.

rubrics_metrics.name: <220> Feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave blank after <220>. <221>-<223> provide for a description of points of biological significance in the sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M) under conditions: if 'n', 'Xaa', or a modified/unusual L-amino acid or modified base was used in a sequence; if ORGANISM is 'Artificial Sequence' or 'Unknown'; if molecule is combined DNA/RNA.

rubrics_metrics.name: <221> Name/Key
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide appropriate identifier for feature, from WIPO Standard ST.25 (2009), Appendices E and F to this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M) under indicated conditions; provide the feature identifier/key.

rubrics_metrics.name: <222> Location
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify location within sequence; where appropriate, state number of first and last bases/amino acids in feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M) under specified conditions (see <220>).

rubrics_metrics.name: <223> Other Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Other relevant information; four lines maximum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M) under certain conditions (see <220>); optional (O) otherwise. Use four-line maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: <300> Publication Information
rubrics_metrics.description: General publication citation information for references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional (O) generally; includes structured subfields (<301>-<307>, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: <301>-<307> Publication subfields
rubrics_metrics.description: <301> Authors; <302> Title; <303> Journal; <304> Volume; <305> Issue; <306> Pages; <307> Date (specify as yyyy-mm-dd, MMM-yyyy or Season-yyyy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors: preferably max. of 10 named authors, one name per line; preferred format Surname, Other Names/Initials. Subfields are optional (O) except when required by context; provide dates and formatting as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: <308> Database Accession Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Accession number assigned by database, including database name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional (O). Provide database name and accession number.

rubrics_metrics.name: <309> Database Entry Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Date of entry in database; specify as yyyy-mm-dd or MMM-yyyy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional (O).

rubrics_metrics.name: <310>-<312> Patent citation dates/numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: <310> Patent Document Number (for patent-type citations only, e.g., US 09/999,999); <311> Patent Filing Date (yyyy-mm-dd); <312> Publication Date (yyyy-mm-dd).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional (O) for general publication fields; mandatory (M) for patent-type citations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: <400> Relevant Residues/Sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: FROM (position) TO (position) and the actual sequence; SEQ ID NO should precede the sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory (M). Provide positions and sequences as required; sequence text should follow the format rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of prior art citations during inter partes reexamination (§1.902)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations by the patent owner and by a third party requester will be entered in the inter partes reexamination file; other citations submitted after the order will be delayed until conclusion of the proceeding, and ex parte reexamination processing is per §1.510/§1.502.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §1.933, §1.915, §1.948, and §1.501 for processing; timing of entry differs by party and stage of proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers on parties (§1.903)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester after a request must be served on every other party in the reexamination proceeding in the manner provided in §1.248; the document must reflect service or it may be refused consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to serve may result in refusal of consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of filing in Official Gazette (§1.904)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of the filing of a reexamination request will be published in the Official Gazette and is constructive notice of the inter partes reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication under §1.11(c) is deemed constructive notice and the proceeding will proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions by the public after filing (§1.905)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions on behalf of third parties other than third party requesters will not be considered unless in accordance with §1.915 or entered prior to the order; submissions after the order must meet §1.501 requirements or will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions not meeting §1.501 are returned; treatment of late third-party submissions follows §1.501 and §1.902.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reexamination (§1.906)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, for subject matter added or deleted, on the basis of 35 U.S.C. 112; claims may not be permitted to enlarge the scope of the patent; other issues outside (a) and (b) will not be resolved in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other issues are raised during reexamination, the examiner will note them and the patent owner may consider filing a reissue application to have such issues considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes reexamination prohibited limits (§1.907)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an order to reexamine has been issued, the third party requester or its privies may not file a subsequent inter partes reexamination request for that patent until a certificate is issued, unless authorized by the Director; judicial final decisions preclude requesting reexamination on issues raised in that civil action; favorable final decisions in an inter partes reexamination prevent requester/privies from requesting further reexamination on issues they raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes estoppel/limitation on successive requests and effects of court/reexamination final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons eligible and timing for filing (§1.913)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person other than the patent owner or its privies may file a request for inter partes reexamination at any time during the enforceability of a patent that issued from an original application filed in the U.S. on or after Nov. 29, 1999, except as limited by §1.907 and paragraph (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests submitted on or after Sept. 16, 2012 will not be accorded a filing date and will not be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of request for inter partes reexamination (§1.915)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must be accompanied by the fee (§1.20(c)(2)) and include: (1) identification of patent and every claim challenged; (2) citation of patents/printed publications showing a reasonable likelihood the requester will prevail for at least one claim; (3) a statement explaining and pointing out each showing of reasonable likelihood and detailed explanation of pertinency and manner of applying the references to each claim; (4) copies of relied-upon patents/printed publications with English translations of necessary parts; (5) copy of the entire patent (front face, drawings, specification/claims in double column format) and any disclaimers/corrections/reexamination certificates; (6) certification that a copy of the request was served on the patent owner (name and address of party served) or duplicate supplied if service impossible; (7) certification that estoppel provisions of §1.907 do not prohibit the reexamination; (8) statement identifying the real party in interest sufficient to determine privy status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed by an attorney/agent identifying another party, power of attorney or representative capacity per §1.34 is required. Failure to include fee or meet requirements will result in notice and opportunity to complete; failure to comply will result in no filing date and placement of the request in the patent file as a citation if it meets §1.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date of request (§1.919)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date is the date on which the request satisfies all requirements set forth in §1.915; if not granted a filing date, the request will be placed in the patent file as a citation if it complies with §1.501.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes when the request is 'filed' for procedural deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner determination timeframe and standard (§1.923)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months following the filing date, the examiner will determine whether the request and prior art establish a reasonable likelihood that the requester will prevail with respect to at least one challenged claim. The determination is based on the claims in effect at the time and will be mailed to the patent owner and requester. If the examiner finds no reasonable likelihood, the request is refused and no reexamination is ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-month statutory consideration period; determination becomes part of official file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial refund if not ordered (§1.925)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where inter partes reexamination is not ordered, a refund of a portion of the fee for requesting inter partes reexamination will be made to the requester in accordance with §1.26(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refund procedure per §1.26(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to review refusal (§1.927)
rubrics_metrics.description: The third party requester may seek review by petition to the Director under §1.181 within one month of the mailing date of the examiner’s determination refusing to order reexamination; any such petition must comply with §1.181(b). If no timely petition is filed or petition is denied, the determination is final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-month deadline; follow §1.181(b) content and form requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order for inter partes reexamination (§1.931)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reasonable likelihood is found, the determination will include an order for inter partes reexamination; if the order resulted from a successful petition under §1.927, the reexamination will ordinarily be conducted by a different examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order initiates the formal reexamination proceeding and may reassign examiner when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner duty of disclosure (§1.933)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the patent owner in an inter partes reexamination has a duty of candor and good faith, including a duty to disclose all information known to be material to patentability as set forth in §1.555(a) and (b). The duty is deemed satisfied by filing a paper in compliance with §1.555(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility rests on designated individuals; the Office will not evaluate compliance during reexamination, but unresolved compliance questions may be noted per §1.906(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Office action and general conduct (§1.935 & §1.937)
rubrics_metrics.description: The order for inter partes reexamination will usually be accompanied by the initial Office action on the merits. Proceedings will be conducted with special dispatch and in accordance with §§1.104–1.116 (application examination process) and will result in issuance of an inter partes reexamination certificate (§1.997) except as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All communications directed to merits must be in writing and filed with the Office; certain petitions require accompanying fees (§1.20(c)(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized papers (§1.939)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unauthorized papers filed by any party at any time during the inter partes reexamination will not be considered and may be returned. Unless otherwise authorized, no paper shall be filed prior to the initial Office action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict limitation on filing timing and authorization of papers; returns and non-consideration are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments by patent owner (§1.943 cross-ref)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments by the patent owner in inter partes reexamination are made by filing a paper in compliance with §§1.530(d)-(k) and §1.943.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the cited sections for proper amendment form and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, page, and word limits for responses and briefs (§1.943)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms must comply with §1.52. Responses by the patent owner and written comments by the third party requester shall not exceed 50 pages in length, excluding amendments, appendices of claims, and reference materials. Appellant’s briefs by patent owner and third party requester shall not exceed 30 pages or 14,000 words (excluding appendices); other briefs ≤15 pages or 7,000 words. If page limit exceeded, a certificate stating the number of words is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict page/word limits with specified exclusions; use word-count certificate if exceeding page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and supplemental response criteria (§1.945)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner will be given at least 30 days to file a response to any Office action on the merits. Supplemental responses will be entered only where accompanied by a showing of sufficient cause including: (1) explanation of how §1.111(a)(2)(i) is satisfied; (2) explanation why supplemental response was not presented with the original response; (3) a compelling reason to enter the supplemental response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental material is narrowly admitted; must justify late submission per three-part test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party comments to patent owner’s response (§1.947)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each time the patent owner files a response, a third party requester may once file written comments within 30 days from date of service of the patent owner’s response. Comments are limited to issues raised by the Office action or the patent owner’s response. Time for submitting comments may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third party's comments are single, limited, and time-bound; filing is considered received as of deposit date per §1.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on submission of additional prior art after order (§1.948)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the inter partes reexamination order, third party requester may only cite additional prior art as part of comments under §1.947 or §1.951(b) and limited to prior art: (1) necessary to rebut a finding of fact by the examiner; (2) necessary to rebut a response of the patent owner; or (3) which first became known or available to the requester after the filing of the request. Prior art under (3) must be accompanied by a statement when it first became known or available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tight limits on new prior art after order; requires explanation when newly discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action closing prosecution (§1.949)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon consideration of issues a second or subsequent time, or upon determination of patentability of all claims, the examiner shall issue an Office action treating all claims present in the reexamination, which may be an action closing prosecution. The action shall set forth all rejections and determinations not to make a proposed rejection and the grounds therefor. An action will not usually close prosecution if it includes a new ground of rejection not previously addressed unless necessitated by an amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office action must comprehensively state grounds; closing prosecution triggers limited response options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options after Office action closing prosecution (§1.951)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an Office action closing prosecution, the patent owner may once file comments limited to issues raised in the Office action; comments can include a proposed amendment subject to §1.116 criteria and must be filed within the time set for response. When the patent owner files comments, a third party requester may once file comments responsive within 30 days from service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-time comments are permitted for each side after a closing action; claim amendments are admissible only under §1.116 standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Appeal Notice and expedited stipulation (§1.953)
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering post-closing comments or expiration of time, the examiner shall issue a Right of Appeal Notice unless prosecution is reopened. Parties may stipulate (patent owner + all third party requesters) that issues are appropriate for final action and request expedited Right of Appeal Notice identifying appealable issues and positions. The Right of Appeal Notice is a final action setting forth each ground of rejection and/or final decision favorable to patentability, identification of status of each claim, reasons for decisions, and sets a one-month period to appeal. If no appeal filed, prosecution terminates and a certificate is issued under §1.997.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right of Appeal Notice is final and prohibits amendment in response; expedited notices require concurrence of all parties and clear identification of issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews prohibited (§1.955)
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be no interviews in an inter partes reexamination proceeding that discuss the merits of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merits-related interviews are barred for inter partes reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner extensions of time (§1.956)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time for action by a patent owner will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified. Requests for extension must be filed on or before the day the action is due and must be accompanied by the petition fee under §1.17(g). Mere filing of the request does not effect any extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are discretionary, require timely filing and payment of petition fee; see §1.304(a) for appeal-time extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file timely/appropriate responses (§1.957)
rubrics_metrics.description: If third party requester files untimely or inappropriate comment/notice/brief, it will be refused consideration. If no claims are found patentable and patent owner fails to file timely and appropriate response, prosecution will be terminated and a certificate issued under §1.997 per last Office action. If some claims are found patentable and patent owner fails to timely respond, further prosecution will be limited to claims found patentable at time of failure and to any claims added thereafter which do not expand the scope of those claims. Bona fide substantial attempts with inadvertent omissions may be given opportunity to explain and supply omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences range from refusal to termination or limitation of prosecution; some leeway for bona fide inadvertent omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive terminated prosecution (§1.958)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a response by the patent owner is not timely filed, a petition pursuant to §1.137 may be filed to revive a reexamination prosecution terminated under §1.957(b) or limited under §1.957(c) if the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revival requires showing of unintentional delay and compliance with §1.137.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (§1.959)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals to the PTAB under 35 U.S.C. 134(c) are conducted according to part 41 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow part 41 procedures for appeal content, timing, and form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of jurisdiction and termination after PTAB decision (§1.979)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction passes to the examiner after PTAB decision upon transmittal of the file to carry into effect the decision, subject to each appellant's right of appeal. Upon judgment in the PTAB appeal, if no further appeal is taken, prosecution will be terminated and the Director will issue and publish a certificate under §1.997 concluding the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal to examiner resumes prosecution; finality tied to further appeals (e.g., Federal Circuit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening after final PTAB decision (§1.981)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a PTAB decision has become final for judicial review, prosecution will not be reopened or reconsidered by the primary examiner except under §41.77 and only with written authority of the Director and then only to consider matters not already adjudicated and with sufficient cause shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening is highly restricted and requires Director authorization and new matters not previously adjudicated.
